newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In the toughest warning it has issued to President Nelson Mandela's government, the Clinton administration said it was "deeply concerned" by cabinet's provisional approval of a three billion rand arms sale to Syria, and might be obliged under U.S. law to suspend aid to South Africa.
- The gold price rallied on an announcement that the Dutch central bank had sold 300 tonnes of gold worth $3.6 billion during 1996.

- Finance Minister Trevor Manuel is to launch a "charm offensive" next month to gain the confidence of local market players who may still be sceptical about his ability to deliver on his ambitious macro-econoic strategy.

- Drug company Adcock Ingram will soon complete the first phase of its rationalisation -- after merging with Premier Pharmaceuticals -- with the retrenchment of more than 600 workers, chief exeutive Phil Nortier said.
- Gold strengthened on international markets on Monday as the Dutch central bank announced it had sold 300 tonnes of gold last year.
- Waltons Stationery is set to list its branded office products and furniture divisions separately in the second half of this year.
- Cyril Ramaphosa, the ANC's former secretary-general and now deputy executive chairman of New Africa Investments, has joined the board of First National Bank.

- Multisar Container Transport, a stainless steel tank container investment company, has placed orders worth 54 million rand with Colombus Stainless, signalling the end of a year-long feud between the industry and the giant stainless steel producer.
- At least 80,000 new pupils are expected to flock to schools in Gauteng today, putting further pressure on the Gauteng Department of Education, which id already buckling under severe overcrowding.
